passages.title: CAQM imposes GRAP - III in Delhi - NCR ahead of Diwali as AQI soars to 382 : Here what allowed and restricted
passages.passage:
The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Friday invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi after the average Air Quality Index (AQI) climbed to 382, placing it in the 'very poor' category.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is likely to remain in the 'severe' category between 7 and 9 November. The forecast for the subsequent six days also suggests that pollution levels are likely to fluctuate between the 'very poor' and 'severe' categories.
The air quality in the national capital moved closer to the 'severe' category on Friday, just two days before Diwali, as pollution levels rose and a layer of smog enveloped the city, reducing visibility.
Although Stage III is generally associated with the 'severe' AQI category, the CAQM invoked the measures as a precautionary step. The move comes amid forecasts that pollution levels in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) could turn 'severe' from Saturday, with Diwali celebrations, vehicular emissions, and the peak stubble-burning season expected to add to the pollution burden.
The Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) is a set of emergency measures implemented across Delhi and the NCR to control air pollution. It has four stages, with restrictions becoming progressively stricter as air quality deteriorates.

passages.title: Delhi AQI remains  very poor  a day ahead of Diwali ,  severe  in several areas
passages.passage:
Delhi continued to grapple with 'very poor' air quality on Saturday, with the national capital's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) standing at 364 at 8 am, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
Delhi AQI remains 'very poor' a day ahead of Diwali, 'severe' in several areas
The readings come a day after the Sub-Committee on the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage 3 across Delhi-NCR, two days ahead of Diwali, to prevent further deterioration.
IIT Delhi logged 443, Punjabi Bagh recorded 433, and Narela stood at 409, all in the 'severe' band. Meanwhile, Cantonment Area recorded 315 and Dhaula Kuan stood at 318, with Anand Vihar at 272 in the 'very poor' and 'poor' categories.
According to the India Meteorological Department, misty conditions prevailed at New Delhi-Safdarjung, where the temperature was 17 degrees C at 5.30 am on Saturday, ANI reported.
According to the CPCB, an AQI between 301 and 400 falls under the 'very poor' category, while readings between 401 and 500 are classified as 'severe'.

passages.title: Peter Thiel Says Apple Has Done  Nothing New  Post Steve Jobs
passages.passage:
Peter Thiel says Apple has done 'nothing new' after Steve Jobs
Peter Thiel, evidently, isn't a fan of the iPhone Duo.
In fact, the billionaire PayPal cofounder and tech investor said he hasn't been very impressed with much of anything that Apple has done since its eccentric founder, Steve Jobs, died of cancer in 2011.
"In my telling, it did nothing new after Jobs," Thiel said of the iPhone maker in a September interview with author Walter Isaacson for the "Builder's Podcast," which was released on Thursday.
Though Thiel told Maureen Dowd of The New York Times in 2017 that Apple's era was over, the company's stock price has grown steadily since then.
Thiel didn't pooh-pooh Apple entirely. He called it a "pure, well-run value stock," but lamented what he described as the loss of vision after Jobs' death.

passages.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max : All the differences explained
passages.passage:
Alongside Apple's first foldable iPhone, a new generation of Pro iPhones has arrived, which means it's time to compare the iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. iPhone 17 Pro Max. Other than a smaller Dynamic Island, Apple hasn't changed the overall design much from last year's model, but there are several upgrades on the new iPhone 18 Pro Max, including a variable aperture camera, longer battery life and the new A20 Pro chipset.
This guide breaks down the key differences between the iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro Max, so you can make a more informed decision before placing your pre-order or upgrading to the newer model. So, whether you already own the iPhone 17 Pro Max or are choosing between the two, we'll help you figure out which one makes more sense.
Amid the ongoing RAM crisis, Apple has increased the prices of both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max by $100. This means the iPhone 18 Pro Max now starts at $1,299, compared to the iPhone 17 Pro Max's $1,199 launch price. Unlike the last time Apple raised the Pro Max's price, there's no base storage increase to soften the blow either.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max comes in four color options: Silver, Glacier, Burgundy, and Black. Notably, Black is making a return after being absent from the iPhone 17 Pro lineup. In comparison, the iPhone 17 Pro Max launched in just three colors: Silver, Deep Blue, and Cosmic Orange.

This is 15% more units than what the 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max sold last year during their first week. Of course, they were competing with the vanilla iPhone 17 and the iPhone Air.
This momentum has carried over into actual sales too. According to information by blogger RD Observation, the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have sold approximately 1.3 million units during the first week of availability in China.
But here’s the more impressive stat – sales of the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are 90% of what the whole iPhone 2025 lineup sold in China during the first week of availability. The absence of a new vanilla and a new Air model isn’t hurting Apple’s bottom line, it seems. Anyone who wants a new iPhone now has to get a Pro. And if you don’t, in a few months, Apple will release the new vanilla (and likely the new Air) model.
Interestingly, these estimates point to the iPhone 18 Pro Max as the more popular model of the two – it sold 55.5% of the total. During the pre-order stage it was the other way around – 60% of people picked the smaller Pro.
